sections.h: Land: parks, karts and the wheel
p: Family Kingdom is the oceanfront amusement park, with a boardwalk setting that is hard to beat for a night out. Pavilion Nostalgia Park at Broadway at the Beach carries on the memory of the old Pavilion, which closed after the 2006 season, and the SkyWheel gives you a view from nearly 200 feet up in an enclosed gondola. Myrtle Waves is the water park.
For speed, Broadway Grand Prix, Fun Warehouse, The Track and K1 Speed are the go-kart tracks. Radical Ropes and Soar and Explore (WonderWorks) are the ropes and zipline options.

Parasailing, jet skis, jet boats and wake parks are mostly clustered in Murrells Inlet, Little River and North Myrtle Beach. Companies like Downwind Sails, Express Watersports, Aloha Watersports and New Wave Watersports run parasailing. Shark Wake Park is a cable wakeboard park. Seakart Adventure and Southern Shores Cruises offer jet boat rides and cruises.
If you want to see the coast from above, Oceanfront Helicopters runs tours. Coastal Scuba and Myrtle Beach Shark Tooth Adventures cover the underwater side.

list: Compare trip lengths, group sizes and what is actually included, not just the headline price.
Ask about safety briefings, life jackets and the weather policy. Water activities are weather-dependent.
Check height, weight and age limits before you drive over, especially for ropes courses and rides.
Many attractions are seasonal. Family Kingdom and Myrtle Waves are among those that close for stretches of the year, so confirm that your dates are covered.
